headline: Sara Duterte Trial Puts SALNs Under Scrutiny as Records Show No Cash Declared Since 2019
seoTitle: Sara Duterte SALNs Under Scrutiny in Impeachment Trial | FMB News
seoDescription: Ombudsman records presented at the Senate impeachment trial showed Sara Duterte's declared net worth rising through 2025 while her SALNs listed no cash from 2019 onward.
deck: Ombudsman records presented at the Senate impeachment trial showed Vice President Sara Duterte’s declared net worth rising through 2025 while her SALNs listed no cash on hand or in bank accounts from 2019 onward; cross-examination also exposed limits in the government’s prescribed disclosure form.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Day 25 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial put the contents and structure of her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth under close examination at the Senate.

Karen Batu, officer-in-charge of the Office of the Ombudsman’s Central Records Division, read figures from Duterte’s SALNs showing her declared net worth rising from P7.25 million in 2007 to P65.04 million in 2021 and P98.66 million in 2025.

The records presented in court showed no cash on hand or in bank accounts declared from 2019 through 2025. Batu also testified that the Ombudsman had no record in its central files of Duterte’s 2013 and 2014 SALNs, including an exit SALN for 2013.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Those documentary facts do not by themselves establish concealment or unexplained wealth. The prosecution and defense disagree over what legal significance should be attached to the entries and omissions.

Cross-examination exposed an important limitation in the disclosure system. Batu confirmed that the prescribed SALN form has no separate line for cash and no column for the acquisition cost of business interests. She also explained that the Ombudsman records office primarily acts as a repository and does not independently verify the truth of every declared figure as part of routine filing.

The prosecution argues that Duterte’s financial disclosures and business interests support the impeachment complaint’s allegations involving unexplained wealth and asset declarations. The defense disputes that interpretation and has emphasized the design of the government’s own form.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The proceedings are testing more than one official’s filings. They are also testing how Philippine accountability rules are interpreted when the prescribed form itself does not explicitly ask for some of the information later placed in dispute.

For readers, the distinction is essential: a missing or zero entry may raise questions, but the Senate impeachment court still has to determine what the evidence proves, what the law requires and whether any proven conduct reaches the constitutional standard for conviction.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the Senate’s treatment of the SALN evidence, testimony involving corporate records, and legal memoranda on the disclosure requirements.
The Senate also set a special session to hear legal views on the disputed conviction-vote threshold before the trial resumes its next evidentiary phase.
